decisions.summary: A new sweep share prunes, inside every live profile (pool trees and the mirror included), a unit or incremental directory unread in L7R_CACHE_STALE_HOURS before the profile's own last use and not the newest of its kind.
decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-27 (request.md line 501): cleanup that happens only when a builder worktree is removed never happens on reused trees, and 'our current tooling is not preventing' the disk filling. Pruning inside the reused trees' live profiles answers that guess directly. Line 413 says time saved outranks disk, so nothing may be cleaned that costs time later. The rule keeps the newest of each kind and whatever a no-op build read, and it judges a profile only against its own last use, so an idle profile is never touched. The class rests on the warm-build measurement (0 units compiled on the pruned copy), which was taken on the mirror's tool profile; most of the 83.3 GB comes from the clone and the landing tree.

decisions.summary: Last use is the newest mtime in the entry and the newest atime of any non-.json file in it, chosen over mtime alone and over every atime.
decisions.why: This is a measured design choice for how the prune in line 501 finds stale entries. Each alternative was priced on the real cache: mtime alone takes units that no-op builds still read, which line 413 forbids, and .json atimes are moved by a scan. It narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: L7R_CACHE_STALE_HOURS is 48 h (GUESS), floored at 25 h for relatime, with 30 h and 72 h priced.
decisions.why: A tuning constant inside the requested cleanup. It is labeled GUESS with its alternatives priced. The 25 h floor keeps relatime from making a read entry look unread, which serves line 413.

decisions.summary: A build running elsewhere no longer holds the prune. A live process or a live gate member in the profile holds that profile whole, and take re-checks an entry's last use at removal. The cache's other shares still wait for any build.
decisions.why: 'Never under a running build' at request.md line 229 is marked as the coordinating session's build, not the GM's words. The GM's words (lines 227, 501) ask for cleanup that actually happens, and a hold by any build anywhere is one way it never does. Nothing a live cargo holds is taken: the profile is skipped whole, and an artifact whose fingerprint was read since the plan is kept.

decisions.id: T515-D5 held eviction keeps its hourly stamp
decisions.summary: When a build holds the rest of the low-disk eviction, the eviction still writes its hourly stamp instead of retrying at every prompt.
decisions.why: Line 227 asks for an automatic trigger below a free-space percentage. The trigger stays, and the prune share still runs under it. Retrying at every prompt would repeat a cache walk of about 20 s each time, and line 413 says time outranks disk. The held shares wait up to an hour, and the trigger is not dropped.

decisions.id: T515-D6 scratchpad half filed as T517
decisions.summary: A landed task's t<N>-* scratch worlds (21.8 GB) are not taken here. T517 is filed for them and lands before T518.
decisions.why: This is sequencing, not an exception. The work is unconditional and owned: filed, ordered before T518, and stated in the found-and-left form that the accepted spec's FR-009 prescribes (why, filed id, order). Nothing in line 501 is dropped or made conditional. The larger share (about 85 GB) lands first.

decisions.id: T515-D7 budget and idle pool-tree profiles left to T518
decisions.summary: After the prune the cache stays about 162 GB against its 100 GB budget. A pool tree's coverage profiles idle for days are taken by nothing, and taking them is to be priced in T518, which lands after T517.
decisions.why: This leaves part of the over-budget cache in place, which narrows line 501's 'leaving things around'. The ground is that the GM's own words already imply it. Line 413: 'If things rarely use that one coverage, but then it saves us a ton of time when they do, then we probably don't want to clean it just because it's been idle for a bit ... we definitely don't want to clean things up if it is going to cost us time later.' Taking an idle pool profile without first pricing what its rebuild costs is exactly what that forbids. The 100 GB figure is the session's build (line 229), not the GM's. The residual is filed and ordered (FR-009 form). This ruling covers only the pricing-first deferral: T518 must still decide on the measured cost, and no ruling here exempts the residual permanently.

decisions.why: His own words: no backfill 'for literally every past task', but the overnight runs 'starting at 11:30 p.m. Eastern last night'. 04:30Z is 23:30 EST.

decisions.why: Carries 'lines added / deleted / modified ... breaking that down by test lines and non-test lines'. Marking shared commits discloses the double count instead of inventing a split, leaving out tick commits drops bookkeeping that is not the task's diff, and splitting prose out of non-test refines his split without removing anything from it.

decisions.why: This narrows the test/non-test split he asked for. His own words limit it ('if doing that can be done relatively cheaply', 'without it being a huge cost'): separating inline test modules means reading each file at each commit to place each hunk. The project keeps its tests in tests/, tests.rs and *_tests.rs files, which are counted as tests, and every task's section says how many of its files have inline tests, so a reader checking how reasonable the figures look can see where the split is rough. It serves his stated purpose rather than defeating it.

Tokens follow from his same-morning words that tokens matter as much as throughput. The SOURCES line supports his 'see whether it seems to include everything'.

decisions.why: This adds to what was asked and narrows nothing. The plan cites the GM's words for it at commit 1da544e1dc, which this bundle's request.md does not hold, so the citation could not be checked here. It is a way of presenting figures he did ask for, to make 'eyeball how reasonable' easier.

The tasks'-side row follows his blocking amendment the same afternoon (keep the denominators separate).

A bundle's commit counts whole under each task it names, marked shared. Tick commits are left out.

The two-table form answers his T243 ask for minutes and, separately, minutes spent blocking.

decisions.summary: The own path is clipped to a builder's Agent::spans, so a builder's stopped stretch (its own background review or test running while it waits) is no part of its path. Whether that wait should count is deferred to T516 ('the brief rules the stopped stretch off the path, and whether that wait shows as its own row is the session's to decide').
decisions.why: The GM's definition of blocking, request.md 2026-11-25 (l), is the standard the own path claims to follow ('each second is booked once, to what its next step waited on'): 'a minute should count as blocking. When something else is waiting on it to be done before it can be started', and it stays blocking 'even if there was a different unrelated task happening in a different subagent at the same time'. A builder stopped on its own background review is a task whose next step waits on that review, so by his definition those minutes block. Nothing in request.md takes an agent's stopped time off the blocking picture. FR-002 (first sentence only, from spec-index.md) books a wait between turns to the background run in flight, and the clip does the reverse for the own path. None of the three grounds holds. The wait can be counted: the build half's unclipped run counted it. His words do not imply leaving it out, and counting it does not defeat the purpose. The stated reason, the session's own brief and 'the session's to decide', is not a ground at all. It is an open question filed in place of an exception. Unlike T513, T514 and T511, whose fixes lie outside this report, this fix sits inside T512's own new figure. The plan's earlier CLEAR rested on the old D6 sentence 'most review-agent time ran where no builder waited on it'. The new D6 says the reverse: most of the difference is 'reviews a builder waited on while stopped'. So that verdict does not carry over. The plan also contradicts itself. Checklist item 12 still calls the clipped stretch 'a stopped builder's background run' misread 'as time it waited', the parallel non-bottleneck the GM worried about. D6 and the T516 item call the same stretch a real wait. Both cannot hold for the same minutes. As written, the 4.9% review figure on the own path tells the reader that review rarely blocked the builders, which the plan's own text disputes. That is the 'technically correct ... but misleading' reading the GM objected to on 2026-11-27. (The 'most of the difference' share is the plan's attribution and was not measured: 214.8 comes from the build half's 83-task run and 87.4 from the current run. This ruling rests on what the plan defers, not on how big the wait is.) What clears it: count a builder's stopped wait on its own background review or test as its task's blocking in this task, on the own path or as a named row of it, and reconcile item 12 and D4's 'so a builder's stopped stretch ... is no part of its path'. Alternatively, put the GM's own words ruling such waits off the blocking picture in request.md.

decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-27 (request.md line 501): cleanup that happens only when a builder worktree is removed never happens on reused trees, and 'our current tooling is not preventing' the disk filling. Pruning inside the reused trees' live profiles answers that guess directly. Line 413 says time saved outranks disk, so nothing may be cleaned that costs time later. The rule keeps the newest of each kind and whatever a no-op build read, and it judges a profile only against its own last use, so an idle profile is never touched. The class rests on the warm-build measurement (0 units compiled on the pruned copy), which was taken on the mirror's tool profile; most of the 83.3 GB comes from the clone and the landing tree.

decisions.summary: Last use is the newest mtime in the entry and the newest atime of any non-.json file in it, chosen over mtime alone and over every atime.
decisions.why: This is a measured design choice for how the prune in line 501 finds stale entries. Each alternative was priced on the real cache: mtime alone takes units that no-op builds still read, which line 413 forbids, and .json atimes are moved by a scan. It narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: L7R_CACHE_STALE_HOURS is 48 h (GUESS), floored at 25 h for relatime, with 30 h and 72 h priced.
decisions.why: A tuning constant inside the requested cleanup. It is labeled GUESS with its alternatives priced. The 25 h floor keeps relatime from making a read entry look unread, which serves line 413.

decisions.summary: A build running elsewhere no longer holds the prune. A live process or a live gate member in the profile holds that profile whole, and take re-checks an entry's last use at removal. The cache's other shares still wait for any build.
